findings.text: follow-on: _success returns True for any outcome beginning with `review scored ` without reading the score value, so a low-scoring review counts as a success in the success-rate and calibration figures; the rule is stated but a threshold would make the success label match the outcome it claims to measure.

follow-on: the after_suite records revision ef9d4155 while the reviewed head is 827c8bdb; the later commit is docs-only so the measured code is unchanged and the delta stands, but a reader reconciling the added-failure count against the reviewed head should know the gate ran on the parent commit.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit; outcomes.py +429 and tests/test_picker_outcomes.py +299 carry the change, cli.py +30 wires the flag, dispatch.py +58 edits only the BudgetHold hold path, SKILL.md and test_skill_contracts.py are the minimal flag edits, plus the evidence fragment and svg.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done_when names a live reading since 2026-10-03T03:00Z published to the evidence fragment with one figure; picker-outcomes.html:1 cites 14 projects and 224 selections and the success-by-confidence figure is committed.
item_verdicts.goal: the node goal is to judge the picker by its own decision outcomes readable from the CLI; reckon/crew/picker/outcomes.py:149 derives mechanics, matched-route outcomes, calibration, offered spend and holds, and reckon/cli.py:1404 exposes them on `reckon crew pick --outcomes`.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it records base 194 passed and head 200 passed, both EXIT=0, the negative control (2 failed, EXIT=1), and names both gate logs.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the manifest declares 8 exclusive paths; the base..head diff changes exactly those 8 across ef9d4155 (feat) and 827c8bdb (docs).

justifications.durability: tests/test_picker_outcomes.py:70 asserts the success rule, calibration buckets, fallback grouping, route-mismatch exclusion, empty/malformed rows and the end-to-end dispatch hold, each against fixture-derived values; the declared negative control (invert) reddens the two known-outcome tests, so the guarded behaviour is shown to fail when reverted.
justifications.evidence: base-gate.log and head-gate.log give 194 to 200 passed with EXIT=0 and the production added-failures deriver over those two logs yields count 0; negative-control.log shows EXIT=1 with the two known-outcome tests red; live-outcomes.json reconciles with every figure in picker-outcomes.html; the one caveat is that the head log's revision is ef9d4155 while the reviewed head is 827c8bdb, a docs-only commit (see finding).
justifications.fit: outcomes.py follows the picker package and ledger idioms with module-scope constants (SUCCESS_RULE, BUCKETS, BURN_LEVELS), and the naming checks record no label or prose hit in the two authored files; the module docstring states the success rule and the route-mode limitation.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/picker/outcomes.py:149 summarize returns rules, mechanics (actions, fallback kinds, latency p50/p90), routed_outcomes, calibration, metered_spend and holds, and reckon/cli.py:1404 emits the same payload as JSON from the existing pick verb.
justifications.scope_discipline: every path in the base..head diff is one of the 8 declared write paths, and reckon/crew/dispatch.py:6296 changes only the BudgetHold branch that records a picker hold, the one edit the brief permits there.
